title: Grattan Institute estimates each unexpected extra 100,000 migrants lifts rents by about 1 per cent, and that cutting net migration to 160,000 would leave rents about 6 per cent lower after a decade
oneLiner: The best-known estimate of how much migration moves rents: real, and modest.
body: Grattan's analysis of the Coalition's 2025 pledge found that holding net overseas migration at 160,000 a year would leave rents about 6 per cent lower than otherwise after ten years, and that cutting permanent skilled visas alone would leave them about 2.5 per cent lower, at a significant cost to incomes. It also noted the federal government has little direct control over net migration, which is driven by uncapped temporary visas.
contextBackground: This figure is cited by both sides: supporters of a cap as proof the effect is real, opponents as proof it is small relative to supply measures.
contextDisagreement: Agreed as Grattan's estimate. Disputed is whether a 6 per cent rent difference after a decade is worth the economic cost Grattan also estimates.

evidenceItems.citation: Grattan Institute, 'Cutting permanent migration may make housing cheaper, but it will definitely make us poorer'

otherClaim.title: Net overseas migration should be held below 200,000 a year

claimItself.title: Net overseas migration should be held below 200,000 a year
claimItself.oneLiner: Whether the federal government should cap net arrivals below the levels of the past decade and well below the post-pandemic peak.
claimItself.body: Net overseas migration is arrivals minus departures of people who stay, or leave, for at least twelve months. It averaged just over 200,000 a year in the decade before the pandemic and exceeded 500,000 in 2022–23. The proposal is a cap of 200,000, which would require the government to manage the student, temporary-work and permanent programs together to hit it.

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: New housing completions have not kept pace with population growth in Australia's largest cities over the past decade

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Holding net overseas migration below 200,000 would require large cuts to international student numbers
